idiom_name: object declaration (exactly one instance, created lazily)
implementation_notes: In Scala the pattern is a declaration: object Config defines a class with exactly one instance, created lazily on first reference like a lazy val, and the JVM turns it into a holder with a static MODULE$ field, so no getInstance() and no private constructor are involved. Objects also replace static members, which is why utility methods and factories live in one. Only top-level objects are global singletons: a nested object is path-dependent (one per enclosing instance), and a companion object is a companion for statics, not a singleton of the class.
pitfalls: An exception thrown while the object initialises leaves it unusable for the process (later access fails), so initialisation should be cheap and total.
A nested object is path-dependent: milk.NutritionInfo and juice.NutritionInfo are distinct values, not one process-wide instance.
Objects are per class loader and their mutable state is global: prefer immutable vals, and remember that only initialisation - not later access - is synchronised.
Mixing a trait with vals into an object makes initialisation order observable; use defs or lazy vals when the order matters.
